Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:40: Let us return to the discourse. It is further said there, in the Tikkunim (66a): "'set me as a seal' - this is the soul [neshamah], which is engraved on the Throne; at the time it is aroused below in prayer, the Throne is aroused above. 'As a seal' - this is 'ruach,' which is the form of the Shin engraved among the angels; at the time it is aroused below in prayer, the angels are aroused with it above. 'Upon your arm' - this is 'nefesh,' which is engraved in the four directions of the world; at the time it is aroused in prayer below, the four directions of the world are aroused with it. 'Neshamah' is the seal; 'ruach' is the shape of the letters that are engraved in the seal; 'nefesh' is the imprint of the letters in the seal, which are marked in the features of a person like the imprint of a seal on a document - and by that imprint of the 'nefesh,' the countenance in a person's body becomes known, in whatever place it is" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:41: It remains for us to explain, in this chapter, the matter of the blemish of the Shechinah with which we began. It is said in the Tikkunim (52a), in these words: "another interpretation: (Genesis 27:4), 'and make me savory food, such as I love' - from the positive commandments, and not 'as I hate,' from the negative commandments. The negative commandments depend on the fear that is [in] Yirah [Malchut], and they serve to keep Satan far from them, so that he does not draw near the Throne, which is the heart, to demand judgments against the holy limbs, who are Israel, and [to keep] the Shechinah dwelling among them" - to this point. The intent is that the negative commandments are all fences to prevent Samael from entering within holiness to arouse judgments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:42: It is further explained in the Tikkunim (55a), in these words, concerning the level [of] "two savory foods": "what are the two savory foods? Rather, after he ascends to his level, he will say to Israel, 'and make me savory food, such as I love' - from the positive commandments, comprised in the Heh of Abraham, which comprises two hundred forty-eight commandments, through which the Heh draws near to the Vav; and this offering is the drawing-near of the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shechinah. The positive commandments are given from the right, and the negative commandments from the left, and these are the two savory foods. The positive commandments are the foods of the Holy One, blessed be He; the negative commandments are the sustenance of Samael for one who transgresses them. It was for these that Esau drew near to Isaac and said to him (Genesis 27:31), 'let my father arise and eat of his son's game' - and Samael, for their sake, would draw near to the left, to give the Holy One, blessed be He, a taste from the sins of their children, which are bitter foods - concerning which it is said (Malachi 1:3), 'but Esau I hated'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:43: It is explained that the positive commandments are the foods of the Holy One, blessed be He, because every commandment effects a union and causes the drawing forth of spiritual, holy flow from the side of kindness; and whoever transgresses a negative commandment breaches a fence, and causes Samael to enter above to arouse the attribute of judgment from the side of Gevurah, so that his portion is bestowed upon him; and since judgment is bestowed through the Shechinah, she tastes from it - and this is "to give the Holy One, blessed be He, a taste from the sins of their children, which are bitter foods" - meaning that they cause the arousal of the bitterness of judgment from the left side. The secret of this bitterness is explained by my teacher, and the matter of this tasting of bitterness is explained (see Pardes, Gate of the Soul, chapter 11).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:44: Further, Rashbi explains (Acharei 74a), in these words: "Rabbi Yehuda said: at a time when the meritorious increase in the world, the Assembly of Israel [Knesset Yisrael] rises with good scents and is blessed from the Holy King, and her face shines; and at a time when the wicked increase in the world, as it were, the Assembly of Israel does not rise with good scents, and she tastes from the bitter, other side - then it is written (Lamentations 2:1), 'He has cast down from heaven to earth,' and so on, and her face is darkened. Rabbi Yosi said: at a time when the meritorious increase in the world, it is written (Song of Songs 2:6), 'his left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me'; and at a time when the wicked increase in the world, it is written (Lamentations 2:3), 'He has drawn back His right hand.' Rabbi Chizkiyah said, from here (Proverbs 16:28), 'and a talebearer separates close friends' - meaning, he separates the King from the Matrona; this is [the meaning of] (Leviticus 18:7), 'the nakedness of your father, and the nakedness of your mother, you shall not uncover.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:45: It is thus explained how great the blemish is, in its various aspects - whether what pertains to the Shechinah, tasting bitterness and having her face darkened, and the reason her face is darkened is because "a foolish son is the grief of his mother" (Proverbs 10:1), as is further explained there below - for he ought to be disciplined, as it says (Proverbs 31:1), "the words of Lemuel the king, the oracle with which his mother instructed him" - and it says that the King never strikes a person directly, but leaves everything in the hand of the Matrona to govern the palace, to discipline the son and lead him in the true way before the King; and when the son conducts himself properly, he is called "a wise son [who] makes his father glad" - "father" here meaning the One who is above all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:46: And it says there: when King Solomon composed the Song of Songs, what great joy was made above! And when he built the Temple, a supernal union was effected above, and all the worlds were in joy and radiance of countenance; and it says, and why all this? Because it is written, "with which his mother instructed him" - for she led him to the King's favor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:47: And it says: and when this person, as I have said, is not led to the King's favor, then it is a nakedness of everything, a nakedness on every side - for the King separates from the Matrona, and the Matrona is distanced from His palace - to this point. This is the aspect of "a talebearer separates close friends," that the blemish reaches even the King, causing Him to be separated from His palace - and this is "the nakedness of your father," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:48: And so it is also explained in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar 16b), in these words: "another interpretation: (Proverbs 16:28), 'a perverse man sends forth strife' - what is meant by 'sends forth'? He sends forth to those plantings [the six extremities], strife that they nurse from the side of judgment. 'And a talebearer separates close friends' - as we have said, the wicked cause a blemish above; 'separates' - the union is not found; he separates the Matrona from the King and the King from the Matrona, and therefore He is not called 'One' - for 'One' is said only when they are in a single union. Woe to those wicked ones who cause separation above! Happy are the righteous, who maintain the [supernal] establishment" - to this point. This is a second aspect concerning the blemish that reaches Tiferet: that all six extremities, called "plantings," all nurse from judgment, as it says, "sends forth strife."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:49: Further, concerning the blemish that reaches the Shechinah, Rashbi explains (Bereshit 22a) that the matter of "a foolish son is the grief of his mother" is because through her the creation of man from the beginning was such that he was composed of good and evil, and therefore she is the one who bears the shame from her son.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:50: Further, it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Korach 178b), in these words: "the Shechinah - whoever does kindness with her, there is no measure to his reward; and whoever sins against her, there is no measure to his punishment" - to this point. And further, in Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Tzav (28b), on the verse (Leviticus 6:6), "a perpetual fire shall burn on the altar" - concerning [the teaching that] a transgression does not extinguish Torah, but a transgression does extinguish a commandment - it says: whoever commits a transgression, which extinguishes a commandment, which is a candle, thereby extinguishes his own candle, of which it is said (Proverbs 20:27), "the candle of the LORD is the soul of man" - the extinguishing is from his own body, so that the body remains in darkness; and likewise, whoever removes the Shechinah from her place causes an extinguishing for the whole world and darkness for that place - and darkness is transgression, "and a maidservant when she supplants her mistress" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:51: The reason is as explained above, in the passage we cited from the Tikkunim, that the Shechinah comprises all the supernal sefirot, all forms of being, all Names, all souls, the Throne, the angels, and so on - everything is portrayed within her. We find, then, that when a person does good deeds toward her, he does kindness with all the worlds comprised within her, all of which shine, and the branches of the Sefirah planted within her arouse their supernal roots that are in the male, so that they arouse the drawing down of mercy and flow from the very highest heights, through the cause of all, blessed be He - and therefore there is no measure to his reward. And when, Heaven forfend, he causes a blemish, the blemish reaches all the realities within her, all of which turn to judgment, causing the extinguishing of light for all the worlds and the rule of darkness, a maidservant in place of her mistress - and therefore there is no measure to his punishment. May God, in His mercy, grant us the merit to be among those who do kindness with her, Amen.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:1: This chapter will explain the remaining aspects of the blemish. There is also a blemish in Tiferet, and this is explained in the Zohar (Yitro 85b), in these words: "we have learned: all the commandments of the Torah are unified in the body of the King - some in the King's head, some in the body, some in the King's hands, and some in His feet, and there is nothing that goes outside the body of the King."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:2: And in these same words, it is cited in the Tikkunim (131a): "and therefore, whoever transgresses the commandments of the Torah is as one who transgresses against the body of the King, as it is written (Isaiah 66:24), 'and they shall go forth and look upon the corpses of the men who transgressed against Me' - against Me literally! Woe to the wicked who transgress the words of the Torah and do not know what they are doing! Rabbi Shimon said: that very place against which he sins, that very place reveals his sin. And Rabbi Shimon said: the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself literally reveals his sin - he sins against the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Holy One, blessed be He, [Himself] reveals his sin, as it is written (Job 20:27), 'the heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him' - 'the heavens shall reveal his iniquity,' this is the Holy One, blessed be He; 'and the earth shall rise up against him,' this is the Holy One, blessed be He [in another aspect]. It is taught: the heavens reveal a person's sin, and at the time it is revealed, the earth executes judgment against the person, as it is written, 'and the earth shall rise up against him,' to execute judgment upon him" - to this point. His words are self-explanatory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:3: From the totality of his words we derive one aspect of fear: that one must fear not to sin, for the King, even though He now shows him a cheerful face and does not immediately show anger, nevertheless it is the King's way to conceal judgment within Himself, and afterward exact full payment - as is explained in Parashat Beshalach (51b), on the reason why the verse "vayet" [and he stretched out, Exodus 14:21] - which corresponds to Tiferet - is written entirely straight [in the Torah scroll's letters], and not half-straight, half-inverted; and they resolved that it is the King's way to conceal judgment. The fool, seeing the King's cheerful face, sins and is not on guard against His judgment; but the wise one says, even though the King's face is cheerful, He keeps judgment within Himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:4: This is [the meaning of] "the heavens shall reveal his iniquity" - for in the future they will reveal what was hidden. "And the earth shall rise up against him" - for she is the one who exacts vengeance for the covenant, and there are two vengeances: one for what he blemished in her, and one corresponding to what he blemished in Him [Tiferet], in the manner of "a talebearer separates close friends," as explained. And the Mother is at first silent even though he has blemished, because "a foolish son is the grief of his mother," until the Father comes and reveals the blemish in the limb with which he blemished - and then she rises up against him to discipline him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:5: Similarly, Rashbi explains (Vayikra 23b), on the verse "and the earth shall rise up against him" - in these words: "Rabbi Yehuda opened [with the verse] (Leviticus 4:23), 'or his sin, which he has sinned, is made known to him' - made known to him from whose side? It should have said, 'or he knows his sin'! What is meant by 'made known to him'? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, commands the Assembly of Israel to make known to the person that sin which he has sinned - and how does He make it known to him? Through her judgments, as it says, 'the heavens shall reveal his iniquity and the earth shall rise up against him.' 'Made known to him' - as He commanded elsewhere, for we have learned: at the time a person sins before the Holy One, blessed be He, and pays no heed to his sin to return in repentance before his Master, but casts it behind his shoulder - his very soul ascends and testifies before the Holy One, blessed be He; then the King commands the Assembly of Israel and says, 'or his sin, which he has sinned, is made known to him' - stretch forth judgment upon him and make his sin known to him, as in (Ezekiel 16:2), 'make known to Jerusalem her abominations.' After judgment reaches him, then his spirit is aroused to return in repentance before his Master and to humble himself to offer a sacrifice - for whoever is arrogant of heart sins and forgets his sin and pays no heed to it, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is ready against him and commands that this sin be made known to him, so that it not be forgotten by him" - to this point. His intent is that the attribute of "O" [the Hebrew "or," meaning "or," whose numerical value is seven] is what makes a person's sin known to him, and "made known" is a command from the Holy One, blessed be He, to her [Malchut], that she make the sin known to the person.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:6: Similarly, it is explained in the Zohar (Chukat 180b) that one must fear the judgment that is in the Shechinah, for at first her face shines upon a person, and afterward she strikes and kills. It says there that the Shechinah is called "the bent Nun," and it says afterward: why is she called this? Rather, as it is said (Leviticus 25:17), "and you shall not wrong [tonu] one another" - for now her face shines and she does wrong [ona'ah] to people, and afterward she strikes like a serpent and destroys and kills, and [yet] she says, "I have done no wrong [avel]" - to this point. Concerning this King Solomon, peace be upon him, commanded (Proverbs 20:2), "the king's terror is like the roaring of a lion; whoever provokes him to anger sins against his own soul" - as if to say, he becomes liable for his own soul, as they said in the Mishnah (Avot 3:4), "he becomes liable for his own soul"; and concerning this it also says (ibid. 24:21), "fear the LORD, my son, and the king."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:7: Further, it says there (Yitro 85b): when the Mother sits upon the children, all the worlds are in joy and completeness; when the Mother is removed, they are all removed from their place - and it is written (Deuteronomy 22:6), "do not take the mother [bird] with the young"; and we have learned: a person should not commit sins below, which cause the Mother to be removed from over the children - to this point. It is thus explained that the blemish reaches even to removing the Mother from over the children, who are the six extremities.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:8: Further, it is explained in the Tikkunim (8a) that sometimes the blemish reaches all the letters of "the LORD," in these words: "and the secret of the matter is that they are able to break through into the letters of His Name - this is [the meaning of] (Exodus 19:21), 'lest they break through to the LORD' - and because they break them through with their sins, they must be rebuilt through their prayer" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:9: Further, concerning the greatness of the blemish, it is further explained in the Tikkunim (17a), in the words of Elijah, in these words: "and because You are within all, whoever separates one from another among these ten [sefirot] is accounted as though he separated within You" - to this point. My teacher, peace be upon him, explained that this is like the parable of one who tears the King's garments from the King - understand this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:10: Further, there is a blemish in the Throne, and this is explained in the Tikkunim (3b), in these words: "of the Shechinah it is said (Song of Songs 1:6), 'do not look at me, for I am dark' - because she is in exile, and her Throne is blemished through the sins of Israel, for there are the souls of Israel. And therefore happy is he who repairs her Throne through his prayers and his commandments, after that Throne has become blemished because of them, and the Name 'the LORD' has withdrawn from there - for it does not rest in a blemished place, as it is said (Leviticus 21:18), 'any man who has a defect shall not draw near'; likewise, it does not rest in a blemished soul. Happy is he who completes his soul so that the Name 'the LORD' rests in it, and makes of it a throne for Himself" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:11: We find, then, that a person blemishes the Throne in three aspects: first, that the Shechinah, when her Throne is blemished, is distressed - because she is the soul clothed within the Throne, and just as distress reaches a soul when the body is blemished, struck, and afflicted because of sins, so too the Shechinah, who is clothed within the Throne, is distressed by the blemishes in the Throne. And it explains that the blemish reaches the Throne because of the root of the souls that are in the Throne - this is "for there are the souls" - and when they [the souls] cause a blemish below, they cause a blemish above, in the Throne.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:12: From this comes a second aspect of blemish: that the souls do not arouse "female waters" [mayin nukvin] to the Shechinah once they have become blemished in the Throne, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:13: The third is that Tiferet, who is "the LORD," the "Adam" who sits upon the Throne, withdraws entirely - this is "and the Name 'the LORD' has withdrawn from there," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:14: Further, Rashbi explains (Behaalotcha 149b) that all sins are portrayed and written upon the Throne, in these words: "at the time judgment hangs over the world and judgments rest, and the Holy One, blessed be He, sits upon the Throne of Judgment to judge the world on that Throne - how many marks are marked upon it, how many hidden records within it, in the wrath of the King! All the books that are opened are stored there, and therefore not a single word is forgotten by the King. And this Throne is not established and does not rest except in the seventh month, which is the day of judgment, the day on which all the people of the world are recorded - they all pass before that Throne" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:15: Further, concerning the blemish that reaches the world of angels, one must fear - for there are seven angels called "the eyes of the LORD, ranging about," and they testify to every blemish portrayed in them, and go and testify before the seventy Sanhedrin. This is explained in the Zohar (Mishpatim 107a), in these words: "it is written (II Chronicles 16:9), 'for the eyes of the LORD range through all the earth' - these are the female [angels]; and it is written (Zechariah 4:10), 'the eyes of the LORD, they range about' - these are the male [angels]; and they are already known. David said (Psalms 51:6), 'and I have done evil in Your eyes [be'eineicha]' - it should have said 'before Your eyes' [lifnei eineicha]! Rather, what is meant by 'be'eineicha'? David said: in that place where I sinned, Your eyes were there - for I knew that Your eyes were present and stood before me, and I did not take them into account. Behold, the sin I committed - in what place was it? In Your eyes."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:16: And so it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Emor 99a): "a guardian angel comes and demands judgment concerning all the deeds of the people of the world, each and every one according to his ways and according to what he has done, and witnesses come and testify concerning all the deeds of the people of the world - and these are 'the eyes of the LORD,' who range through the whole world; and there are countless 'eyes of the LORD' who go about and range through the whole world and see all the deeds of the people of the world. Woe to those who do not take heed and do not consider their deeds - for the King's witnesses stand and go about them and observe them! And this guardian angel stands before the King and demands judgment: so-and-so did such-and-such, so-and-so did thus - and here are the witnesses."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:17: Further, of this kind is that a person causes the impure Samael to enter among the world of the holy angels to teach accusation - will they not say, who caused this stinking impure one to enter among us? Surely he will certainly be punished!
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:18: Further, concerning the blemish pertaining to the angels, it is explained in the Sabba (Mishpatim 106b), on the verse (Isaiah 57:18), "and I will repay comforts to him and to his mourners" - it says that the two angels who always accompany a person to guard him, of whom it is said (Psalms 91:11), "for He shall command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways" - when a person sins, they separate from him and stand mourning over him because of his sin. And when he repents, of whom it is said, "I have seen his ways, and I will heal him, and I will lead him, and I will repay comforts to him" - first, because he has repented and taken comfort over what has passed, and afterward "to his mourners" - these being the angels who stood mourning over him. Therefore it is fitting that a person take to heart not to sin, lest he cause the angels to mourn over him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:19: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in his own Pekudin (Zohar, Naso 123a) that "his mourners" are the two hundred forty-eight commandments that mourn over him, in these words: "all the positive commandments that were destined to rest within his two hundred forty-eight commandments all mourn over him - and the secret of the matter is 'I have seen his ways, and I will heal him,' and so on, 'and to his mourners' - these are the two hundred forty-eight commandments that mourn over him, which are the supernal image that rests upon his head, in which 'the LORD' rests" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:20: Further, concerning the blemish pertaining to the days, our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the Pesikta Rabbati, in these words: "(Proverbs 4:23), 'guard your heart above all that is guarded' - Rabbi Acha said: there are two hundred forty-eight positive commandments in the Torah, corresponding to the two hundred forty-eight limbs of a person, for every single limb cries out to the person, perform a commandment through me so that you may live by its merit and lengthen your days; and there are three hundred sixty-five negative commandments, corresponding to the number of solar days - for every day, from the hour the sun rises until it sets, cries out and says to the person: I adjure you, by the One who has brought your days to this day, do not commit a transgression through me, and do not tip the balance for me and for the whole world to the side of guilt" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:21: Similarly, Rashbi explains (Emor 92a), in these words: "come and see, we have learned: a fast is as beneficial for a bad dream as fire for tow, and the essence of the fast is on that very day, not on another day. Why? Because there is no day below over which another, supernal day does not rule; and when one begins a fast for a dream, we have learned that day does not depart until that decree is annulled - and if he postpones it to another day, that is the dominion of the other day, and a day does not enter into the day of its fellow. In this manner, there is no day that does not have a supernal day appointed over it above, and a person must be careful not to cause a blemish on that day, and not to be blemished before the other days."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:22: And we have learned: through an action below, an action above is aroused. If a person performs an action below properly, so a force is aroused properly above; if a person performs kindness in the world, kindness is aroused above, and it rests on that day and is crowned through it. Because of this, if a person is led to show mercy below, mercy is aroused for that day, and it is crowned with mercy through it, and that day stands by him to be his advocate at the time he needs it - the same pattern in reverse. And above all, if a person performs a deed of cruelty, that day is aroused and blemished, and afterward stands against him with cruelty to destroy him from the world - with the same measure a person measures, he is measured" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:23: Similar to this passage, Rashbi explains (Vayechi 224a) what King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 139:16), "days were formed" - that the days themselves have a formation and a mode of being, in which the soul is clothed after its departure from the world, according to the deeds it performed with them, in these words: "Rabbi Yehuda opened and said (Isaiah 42:18), 'hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see' - 'hear, you deaf' - these are people who do not heed the words of the Torah and do not open their ears to hear the commandment of their Master; 'and the blind' - who do not look to know upon what they stand, for every single day a herald goes forth and calls, and none pay heed. For it is taught: a person's days, when they were created, on the day he came into the world, all of them stand in their own existence and go about flying through the world; they descend and warn a person, each and every day, alone. When that day comes and warns him, and the person commits a sin before his Master on that day, that day ascends in shame and gives testimony, and stands alone, outside. We have learned: after it stands alone, it waits until the person repents from it. If he merits, that day returns to its place; if he does not merit, that day descends and joins with that spirit outside, and returns to its house and takes on the very image of that person, in order to do him harm, and dwells with him in his house - and some [days'] dwelling is for good, if he merits, and if not, its dwelling with him is for evil. Either way, those days are recorded and are lacking, and are not counted among those that remain. Woe to that person who diminishes his days before the Holy King, and does not leave days above to be crowned with them in that world and to draw near with them before the Holy King.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:24: Come and see: when those days draw near before the Holy King, if this person who departs from the world is worthy, he ascends and enters into those days, and they are the garments of honor in which his soul is clothed - and these are the days in which he merited and did not sin. Woe to one who diminishes his days above - for when they wish to clothe him in his days, those days that he blemished through his sins are lacking from that garment, and he is clothed in a deficient vessel; how much more so if they are numerous, so that a person has nothing to be clothed in in that world! Then woe to him, woe to his soul, for they judge him in Gehinnom for those days, day for day, doubled - for when he departs from this world, he finds no days to be clothed in, and has no garment with which to cover himself. Happy are the righteous, whose days are all stored up with the Holy King, and from them are made garments of honor to be clothed in in the World to Come" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:25: And it says afterward that concerning this it is said (Genesis 24:1), "and Abraham was old, advanced in days" - meaning that he entered and was clothed in all his days, which were all properly ordered.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:26: It is thus explained, concerning the punishment of one who does not properly order all his days, that he is judged in Gehinnom day for day, doubled. The reason is that since all a person's days together form a single, complete garment - the complete stature - in which a person prepares his soul to be clothed, any blemish on a single day is a blemish in the entire garment, so that his garment is found torn.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:27: And so it is explained in the Talmud (Chagigah 5b): it says there of Rav Idi, that he would travel three months to study for a single day, and return home for three months; and Rabbi Yochanan expounded concerning him (Isaiah 58:2), "yet they seek Me daily [yom yom]" - whoever occupies himself with Torah even one day a year is as though he occupied himself with it the whole year. And it says, and likewise regarding the measure of punishment, as it is written (Numbers 14:34), "according to the number of days in which you spied out the land" - but did they sin for forty years? They sinned only for forty days! Rather, this teaches you: whoever commits a transgression even one day a year, Scripture accounts it against him as though he transgressed the whole year - to this point.
